identity.real_world_identity_notes: Brazilian customer sports prototype built by Metalmoro, sold in several prototype classes. The manufacturer states the car accepts a choice of engine and gearbox rather than specifying either. Duratec Turbo denotes the Ford engine.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: automatic cut on upshifts and no automatic blip, so the driver supplies the downshift blip.
The clutch is needed to pull away.

Whether a downshift blip is needed to engage a gear was not tested and no reviewed source establishes the gearbox construction, so it stays unknown rather than being inferred from the absent automation.
This P3 configuration differs from its P2 sibling on both counts the drive tested: it needs the clutch to move off and it does not blip its own downshifts. Nothing is inherited between them.

Metalmoro states only that the MRX accepts several engine and gearbox options, so no reviewed source establishes which gearbox this configuration carries. The sequential construction is what the drive showed.
Community references for this car are generated from Coanda's AMS2 spreadsheet, so they describe the simulator rather than the real car and are not cited here as real-world evidence.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.metalmoro-mrx-duratec-turbo-p3.20260817t043659674z-d771315f by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.

claims.basis: The manufacturer's own page establishes the MRX; the class and engine configuration were observed live.
The manufacturer does not state a gearbox, so the six sequential gears and the automatic cut come from the live drive rather than from the source.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

archetype.basis: Two archetypes survive the gap: stick-6-seq-clutch-start-flat-up-blip-down and stick-6-seq-clutch-start-flat-up-no-blip. They differ only on downshift.manual_blip. A guided drive settles it, by downshifting with no throttle input and seeing whether the gear engages.

driver_summary: Six-speed sequential with a lever. The car cuts the upshift, so stay flat. Nothing blips the downshift, and whether this gearbox needs one to engage is not established, so blip anyway: it settles the car into the corner whether or not the box demands it.
